newsitem.title: CHINA: Amnesty urges HK's new rulers to be flexible.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty urges HK's new rulers to be flexible.

text.p: Amnesty International on Tuesday urged Hong Kong's new authorities to show tolerance toward future street protests once world attention shifts away from the former British colony.

But it was unfortunate that Hong Kong people would have their political freedoms curtailed by a Beijing-anointed provisional legislature, Rory Mungoven, asia director for the London-based rights group, told Reuters.
He was speaking just after Britain handed the territory back to China at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday.
Mungoven said peaceful pro-democracy protests in the streets of Hong Kong that coincided with the formal handover showed the maturity of Hong Kong politics.

"This really underlines the peaceful and orderly nature of Hong Kong politics. It's good that the new authorities showed flexibility tonight, let's hope that continues when the world's media spotlight lifts," he told Reuters.
"It's a shame that ordinary Hong Kong people celebrate their freedoms in such a peaceful way and that their new unelected legislature that will be sitting tonight will be curbing those freedoms."
Pro-democracy activists poured into Hong Kong's streets in the early hours of Tuesday, staging boisterous rallies and vowing to fight for civil liberties after the handover.
Demonstrators expressed anger at curbs which Hong Kong's new chief executive Tung Chee-hwa imposed on political reforms adopted in the twilight of British rule.

The provisional legislature, which was sworn in only hours after the handover and which replaced a chamber elected in 1995, will pass bills rolling back Hong Kong's civil liberties laws among its first order of business.
Mungoven called on the international community to put pressure on Beijing to ensure Hong Kong keeps its freedoms.
"It's important the international community see what's alive in Hong Kong and protect and defend it by keeping up the pressure on China and the new Hong Kong authorities," he said.
